# Synthetic Teaching Fixtures

Source: parent task supplied on 5 September 2026. These are teaching/test fixtures, not publications. No external search or external research claims were requested.

## Q1: Single-Server Queue

Make a 5-minute talk for ML researchers explaining a toy stationary M/M/1 queue. Arrival rate is 6 jobs/s and service rate is 10 jobs/s. Expected system time is 1/(10-6) = 0.25 seconds. Explain why approaching capacity increases waiting. Use the SD slides reference feel.

## T1: Midpoint Theorem

Make a 12-minute theory talk proving that the midpoint minimizes the sum of squared Euclidean distances to fixed a and b. Given identity:

`||x-a||^2 + ||x-b||^2 = 2||x-(a+b)/2||^2 + ||a-b||^2/2`.

Explain assumptions, proof, example a=0 and b=2, uniqueness, and the limitation to squared Euclidean distance rather than an arbitrary metric.

## P1: Adaptive Draft Length Proposal

Make an 8-minute proposal exploring adaptive draft length in a toy LM serving setup. The only supplied concern is that batching may change verification cost. No benchmark or measured improvement is supplied. Proposed validation varies batch load and draft length and reports latency, throughput, and acceptance. Use a fixed-length baseline and token-distribution correctness checks. This is a proposal, not a result paper.

Presenter: Skill QA. Date: 5 September 2026. Sources, PDFs, previews, storyboards, and a concise evidence/QA report remain in this directory. No publishing or installation changes.
